name: Elihu
bio: Elihu son of Barachel, a young Buzite of Ram's family, had listened silently to the whole debate between Job and his three friends out of deference to their age, but grew angry when Job justified himself over God and the friends failed to answer him yet still condemned him. Speaking up at last, Elihu argued across six chapters that suffering is not only punishment but can be God's way of disciplining and refining a person, that God is too great and just to be unfair, and that Job had spoken rashly in demanding to argue his case with the Almighty; he pointed to God's power and wisdom displayed throughout creation as reason enough for humble submission (Job 32-37). His speech leads directly into the LORD's own appearance to Job in a whirlwind.
